Introduction

Quick start

Build a small routiva app step by step, then exercise every endpoint with curl.

What we are building#

One file with a JSON API, request logging, body parsing, a static public/ folder and error handling. Each step adds one piece and explains why. The finished server is about 40 lines.

1. Scaffold the project#

bash
mkdir routiva-app
cd routiva-app
npm init -y
npm pkg set type=module
npm install routiva

npm pkg set type=module writes "type": "module" into package.json, which is required — routiva is ESM-only.

2. Your first route#

Create server.js:

js
import { createApp } from 'routiva';

const app = createApp();

app.get('/', (req, res) => {
  res.json({ hello: 'world' });
});

app.listen(3000, () => console.log('http://localhost:3000'));

Run node server.js and open <http://localhost:3000/>. res.json() sets Content-Type: application/json and serializes the object.

3. Add logging and JSON parsing#

logger() prints one line per request; json() parses JSON bodies into req.body. Register both before your routes:

js
import { createApp, logger, json } from 'routiva';

const app = createApp();

app.use(logger());
app.use(json());

Both call next(), so the request continues to the routes below. Middleware registered after a route cannot run before it — registration order is execution order.

4. Add a parameterized route#

js
app.get('/users/:id', (req, res) => {
  res.json({ id: req.params.id });
});

:id matches a single path segment. /users/42 sets req.params.id to the string '42'; /users/42/posts does not match.

5. Read the query string#

js
app.get('/search', (req, res) => {
  res.json({ q: req.query.q, tags: req.query.tag });
});

req.query is parsed from the URL. Repeated keys become arrays, so ?tag=a&tag=b yields { tag: ['a', 'b'] }.

6. Accept a JSON body#

js
app.post('/users', (req, res) => {
  res.status(201).json({ created: req.body });
});

req.body is populated by json() for application/json requests. Bodies over the 1mb default limit get a 413; malformed JSON gets a 400.

7. Throw an error#

Handlers can throw, and async handlers can reject. Either way the error flows to an error handler. routiva has a default one, but a custom handler is easy to add — four parameters marks it, and it is registered last:

js
import { HttpError } from 'routiva';

app.get('/boom', async () => {
  throw new HttpError(503, 'service unavailable');
});

app.use((err, req, res, next) => {
  res.status(err.status || 500).json({ error: { message: err.message } });
});

Without the custom handler, routiva returns { "error": { "message": "...", "status": ... } } for an HttpError and a generic 500 for anything else.

8. Serve a folder of static files#

Create public/index.html:

html
<!doctype html><html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><title>routiva</title></head><body><h1>Served by routiva</h1></body></html>

Register the middleware after your routes so an explicit route always wins:

js
import { serveStatic } from 'routiva';

app.use(serveStatic('public'));

serveStatic streams files, sets ETag/Last-Modified for 304 responses, honours single Range requests, and falls through to the next layer when a file is missing.

9. The complete server#

js
import { createApp, logger, json, serveStatic, HttpError } from 'routiva';

const app = createApp();

// middleware every request passes through
app.use(logger());
app.use(json());

// routes
app.get('/', (req, res) => {
  res.json({ hello: 'world' });
});

app.get('/users/:id', (req, res) => {
  res.json({ id: req.params.id });
});

app.get('/search', (req, res) => {
  res.json({ q: req.query.q, tags: req.query.tag });
});

app.post('/users', (req, res) => {
  res.status(201).json({ created: req.body });
});

app.get('/boom', async () => {
  throw new HttpError(503, 'service unavailable');
});

// static files fall back for anything the routes did not match
app.use(serveStatic('public'));

// error handler goes last
app.use((err, req, res, next) => {
  res.status(err.status || 500).json({ error: { message: err.message } });
});

app.listen(3000, () => console.log('http://localhost:3000'));

10. Run it and test every endpoint#

Start it with node server.js, then run:

bash
curl http://localhost:3000/
curl http://localhost:3000/users/42
curl "http://localhost:3000/search?q=cats&tag=a&tag=b"
curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/users \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"Ada"}'
curl -i http://localhost:3000/boom
curl -i http://localhost:3000/index.html

What to expect:

RequestResponse
GET /{"hello":"world"}
GET /users/42{"id":"42"}
GET /search?q=cats&tag=a&tag=b{"q":"cats","tags":["a","b"]}
POST /users201 and {"created":{"name":"Ada"}}
GET /boom503 and {"error":{"message":"service unavailable"}}
GET /index.htmlthe HTML file as text/html

GET /missing falls through the static middleware to routiva's default 404 JSON.
